newsitem.title: MEXICO: Hylsamex, Posco in Venezuela venture.
newsitem.headline: Hylsamex, Posco in Venezuela venture.

text.p: Mexican steel maker Hylsamex and majority partner South Korean Posco plan to invest $262 million to construct a plant in Venezuela, Hylsamex said in a statement Wednesday.
"The new plant...will be built beginning next April in Guayana, Venezuela," the company said.
The plant will be built by U.S. Raytheon Engineering and Posec, Posco's engineering division, the statement said.
Hylsamex's technology division, Hylsa, and its U.S. partner Kvaermer-Davy plan to supply technology, corresponding licensing and engineering design for the project.
Posco will be the plant's principal investor with 40 percent of shares, while other Korean firms, Dongbu Steel and Hyundai hold an additional 35 percent, Hylsamex said.
Hylsamex, Raytheon and Venezuelan Ferrominera del Orinoco hold the remaining 25 percent stake in plant.
